title: Dealerships Are DENYING Warranty Claims on New/Used Cars
summary: A creator reacts to clips of dealerships and warranty companies denying claims, showing how CPO warranties, service contracts and manufacturer coverage each find reasons to shift blame elsewhere.

assertions.quote: No, we're not going to cover that because this should be covered under her CPO warranty.

verdicts.note: Coverage disputes between overlapping warranty providers, each denying responsibility, are a commonly reported consumer complaint pattern.

assertions.quote: I have been paying for a warranty that I never really had.

verdicts.note: This is a single anecdote; whether service contracts are commonly voided without notice while payments continue is not established by broad data.

CFPB found servicers financed GAP coverage on salvage-titled vehicles that was void from inception -- delivering no benefit while still increasing what the consumer financed and paid monthly -- though this specific finding is about GAP, not vehicle service contracts.

assertions.quote: it's going to start at zero miles and it's going to essentially double cover you.
a condition that occurred before you purchased this agreement that would have been obvious and apparent if the vehicle had been inspected
they buy a car knowing that it needs all these repairs

verdicts.note: This describes a real, reported dealer tactic, but characterizing dealer intent at scale goes beyond what anecdotal and enforcement cases alone can establish.

assertions.quote: taking the 1,500 hours and multiplying it by the average speed

verdicts.note: Converting idle engine hours into equivalent mileage to argue a warranty has expired is a documented dealer/manufacturer tactic, though its prevalence varies by brand and contract.

assertions.quote: just because you got a manufacturer warranty, it still don't mean that they going to cover everything.

verdicts.note: Manufacturer warranties always carry exclusions for wear items, misuse, aftermarket parts and maintenance lapses, so coverage is narrower than owners often assume.
